# Define tutorial packaging format

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format that makes tutorials versioned
and testable independently of Dashboard releases. The format specifies how a
tutorial is packaged: its metadata, its pinned images, and its validation
manifest. It is the interface that both the tutorial authoring work and the
Dashboard gallery's launch mechanics build against.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial metadata model: the descriptive and structural
  information the Dashboard gallery needs to present a tutorial and launch it
  (e.g., identity, journey classification, entry points for the notebook or
  pipeline artifact).
- Define how tutorial images are pinned so a tutorial executes against known,
  immutable image versions rather than moving tags.
- Define the validation manifest: the machine-readable description of how a
  tutorial is validated, so each tutorial can be tested against the current
  release on its own versioning cadence.
- Define versioning rules for tutorial packages so tutorials can be updated
  and re-tested without a Dashboard release.
- Publish the format as a written specification and a validation mechanism
  that can check a tutorial package for conformance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A written specification of the tutorial packaging format exists covering
  metadata, pinned images, and the validation manifest.
- A sample tutorial package can be expressed in the format and passes the
  conformance/validation mechanism.
- Pinning an image version in a tutorial package is demonstrated and the
  pinned reference is carried through the validation manifest.
- A tutorial package versioned under the format can be validated without a
  Dashboard release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently
  of Dashboard releases.

Note: this epic also transitively enables HLR-1 and HLR-2 (both P0), and
therefore inherits priority P0.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and one-click launch mechanics

## Description

This epic delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated, browsable
gallery of getting-started tutorials from which a user can launch a tutorial
into their own project with one click — opening a workbench with the tutorial
notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline.

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard (navigation entry,
  gallery listing, tutorial detail presentation driven by the tutorial
  packaging format's metadata).
- Implement one-click launch of a notebook-based tutorial into the user's
  project: open a workbench with the tutorial notebook loaded, using the
  pinned image declared by the tutorial package.
- Implement one-click launch of a pipeline-based tutorial into the user's
  project: import the tutorial pipeline into the project's pipeline
  environment.
- Launch targets the user's own project, respecting existing project-scoped
  RBAC.
- Gallery content is driven by tutorial packages conforming to the packaging
  format, so tutorial content can be updated independently of Dashboard
  releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery from the Dashboard and browse the
  curated tutorial set with its metadata.
- Given a notebook-based tutorial, one click opens a workbench in the user's
  project with the tutorial notebook, running the pinned image declared by
  the tutorial package.
- Given a pipeline-based tutorial, one click imports the tutorial pipeline
  into the user's project where it is visible among the project's pipelines.
- Launch works for a user scoped to their own project only (existing RBAC
  respected; no cluster-scoped privileges introduced).
- The gallery renders a tutorial package that conforms to the packaging
  format without Dashboard code changes specific to that tutorial.
- Launching a tutorial into a project where the relevant components are
  enabled works end to end (workbench reaches running state; imported
  pipeline is selectable to run).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can
  launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline).

# Author and test six curated getting-started tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the six curated tutorials covering the core getting-started
journeys — first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline,
first deployment, and first RAG app — and keeps each tested against the
current release. The tutorials are substantive authored content (notebooks
and a pipeline), packaged and validated per the tutorial packaging format so
they are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases.

## Scope

- Author the six tutorials, one per core journey:
  1. First workbench (create a project and workbench, open the notebook).
  2. Data prep (load and prepare data in a workbench).
  3. First training run (train a model in the workbench).
  4. First pipeline (build and run a training/batch pipeline).
  5. First deployment (serve the trained model).
  6. First RAG app (assemble a retrieval-augmented generation example).
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format: metadata filled
  in, images pinned, validation manifest completed.
- Validate each tutorial against the current release using its validation
  manifest, and record results so re-validation after release updates is
  repeatable.
- Fix tutorial content that fails validation against the current release.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Six tutorials exist, one for each core journey listed in scope, each
  packaged per the tutorial packaging format and passing format conformance.
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current release
  (workbench tutorials reach a completed notebook execution; the pipeline
  tutorial's run completes; the deployment and RAG tutorials' served
  endpoints respond).
- Each tutorial declares pinned images, and validation runs against those
  pinned references.
- Tutorial packages carry version metadata, and a re-validation of an
  existing tutorial can be run without a Dashboard release.
- Tutorials contain no placeholder or stub content; each is a complete,
  curated walkthrough of its journey.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first
  workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment,
  first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release.
- HLR-3 (partial support): the tutorials are concrete instances of the
  packaging format (the format itself is defined elsewhere).

Note: this epic's work spans notebook-based tutorials (workbench journeys)
and one pipeline-based tutorial (Data Science Pipelines); the canonical
component assigned is Notebooks as the most-relevant name.

# Document tutorial gallery usage and contribution process

## Description

This epic authors the documentation for the tutorial gallery: how users use
the gallery to launch tutorials into their projects, and how contributors
author and submit new tutorials. Documentation runs last so it describes what
was actually built — the gallery, the launch mechanics, the six tutorials,
and the packaging format.

## Scope

- Author user-facing documentation for using the tutorial gallery: finding
  tutorials, launching a notebook-based tutorial into a workbench, and
  launching a pipeline-based tutorial.
- Author contributor-facing documentation for the tutorial contribution
  process: how to author a tutorial, package it per the tutorial packaging
  format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), validate it against
  the current release, and submit it for curation.
- Document the scope boundary of the contribution process: this release
  documents the process but ships no submission tooling; partner- and
  community-contributed tutorial intake and localization are out of scope.
- Verify all documented steps against the delivered gallery and tutorials.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers using the gallery end to end: browsing the
  gallery, launching a tutorial into a project as a workbench, and importing
  a tutorial pipeline.
- Published documentation covers the contribution process for new tutorials,
  including packaging per the format and validation against the current
  release.
- Documentation is technically reviewed against the delivered implementation
  (gallery behavior, tutorial set, packaging format) by someone who verified
  each documented step, with review evidence recorded.
- Documentation contains no steps or references that fail when followed
  against the delivered release.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution
  process for new tutorials.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
